scorecard.note: Provide a clear, relatable implication or answer to the opening question instead of just restating the statistic.

storyboard.ears: Satellites found an ocean-wide shift larger than researchers expected.
Ocean color changed across 56% of the surface. The shift is already visible at planetary scale.
storyboard.evidence: Nature / MIT (B.B. Cael et al.) | Share of ocean surface that changed color (2002-2022) | https://news.mit.edu/2023/study-oceans-color-changing-climate-change-0712 | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: The model predicted 50% would change color. Satellite observations later exceeded that forecast.
storyboard.evidence: Nature / MIT (B.B. Cael et al.); model by Stephanie Dutkiewicz (2019) | Predicted vs observed share of ocean that would change color | https://news.mit.edu/2023/study-oceans-color-changing-climate-change-0712 | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: Changed ocean color spans 203 million square kilometers. That area is larger than Earth's total land.
storyboard.evidence: Nature / MIT (B.B. Cael et al.) | Area of ocean that changed color vs all land on Earth | https://news.mit.edu/2023/study-oceans-color-changing-climate-change-0712 | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: Ocean color change now covers an area larger than all land on Earth.
